text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.1% today to $134.26, continuing a pullback from last week's peak of $137.20. The decline comes as crude oil prices softened—U.S. oil dropped to $91.48 per barrel—suggesting weaker near-term demand or supply relief concerns, even as diesel prices remain elevated due to ongoing refinery disruptions from the Ukraine and Iran conflicts. The stock has given back about $3 per share over the past three trading sessions after climbing sharply earlier in the week.

The broader geopolitical backdrop remains supportive for oil producers in the longer run: new U.S. sanctions on Iran, potential supply constraints from Russian refinery damage, and efforts to stabilize the Strait of Hormuz all underpin tighter crude markets. Today's modest pullback appears more tactical—a natural correction after a strong rally—rather than a shift in the structural factors that have kept energy prices elevated.
